summary: Thoön (Ancient Greek Θόων) son of Phaenops was a Trojan warrior, twin brother of Xanthus. Diomedes kills both brothers in Iliad 5, leaving their aged father without other sons to tend him — a miniature tragedy inside Diomedes' aristeia.
etymology: Thóōn is a Homeric warrior name borne by several Trojans and allies; this node is fixed by the patronymic Phaenopid.

sections.heading: Sons of Phaenops
paragraphs: Homer (Iliad 5.152–158) has Diomedes slay Xanthus and Thoön, sons of Phaenops. Their father, worn with age, begets no other son after them — the poem's brief pathos for a house ended in one afternoon's fighting.

The atlas id thoon-phaenopid is this Phaenopid. He is not Thoön whom Antilochus or Agamemnon slays elsewhere in the Iliad (thoon-trojan), nor the Giant Thoas/Thoon (thoas-giant), nor the Lycian or Phaeacian namesakes.

sections.heading: Homonyms
paragraphs: Multiple Homeric Thoöns share one Wikipedia disambiguation page. Always prefer the patronymic or killer to keep the nodes apart.
